passages.heading: <frame> HTML frame element
passages.text: Avoid using this feature in new projects. This feature may be a candidate for removal from web standards or browsers. See full compatibility Learn more The <frame> HTML element defines a particular area in which another HTML document can be displayed. A frame should be used within a <frameset>. Using the <frame> element is not encouraged because of certain disadvantages such as performance problems and lack of accessibility for users with screen readers. Instead of the <frame> element, <iframe> may be preferred.

passages.heading: Attributes
passages.text: Like all other HTML elements, this element supports the global attributes. src This attribute specifies the document that will be displayed by the frame. name This attribute is used for labeling frames. Without labeling, every link will open in the frame that it's in – the closest parent frame. See the target attribute for more information. noresize This attribute prevents resizing of frames by users. scrolling This attribute defines the existence of a scrollbar. If this attribute is not used, the browser adds a scrollbar when necessary. There are two choices: "yes" for forcing a scrollbar even when it is not necessary and "no" for forcing no scrollbar even when it is necessary. marginheight This attribute defines the height of the margin between frames. marginwidth This attribute defines the width of the margin between frames. frameborder This attribute allows you to specify a frame's border.

passages.heading: A frameset document
passages.text: A frameset document has a <frameset> element instead of a <body> element. The <frame> elements are placed within the <frameset>. <!doctype html> <html lang="en-US"> <head> <!-- Document metadata goes here --> </head> <frameset cols="400, 500"> <frame src="https://developer.mozilla.org/en/HTML/Element/iframe" /> <frame src="https://developer.mozilla.org/en/HTML/Element/frame" /> </frameset> </html> If you want to embed another HTML page into the <body> of a document, use an <iframe> element.
